title: Audit and eval harness for KV/prefix-cache output stability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Build an automated audit and evaluation harness that detects and triages output divergence caused by KV/prefix cache hits after model/config changes. Background: We've observed cases where cache hits reduce latency and cost but subtly change generated outputs (tokenization offsets, position embeddings, quantization kernel behavior). Existing tickets focus on detection and correctness evals; this ticket centralizes a reproducible harness, metricization, and alerting for cache-induced deltas tied to model version/config rollouts. Goal: prevent silent quality regressions when introducing cache optimizations, new kernels, or model variants by (1) creating deterministic replay + golden-output comparisons, (2) defining delta thresholds and scoring, (3) surfacing failures in the Console and CI, and (4) providing fast rollback/masking mechanisms.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can replay saved request traces deterministically with cache enabled and disabled against the same model+config; 2) Harness produces per-request delta metrics (token-level mismatch rate, semantic embedding distance, top-k logit deltas) and aggregates them per-deploy; 3) Thresholds (P0/P1/P2) are configurable and cause alerts to paging/Slack and mark deploy as failed in canary; 4) CI gate that runs a sampled golden set and blocks PRs that exceed configured severity; 5) Console shows a per-model cache-stability dashboard with trendlines and top offending prompts/clients; 6) Runbook documented for triage and mitigation steps.
repro_steps: 1) Take a representative trace set (1000 prompts) from prod traces with user consents/PII removed; 2) Run trace against current model/config with KV cache enabled; 3) Run same trace with cache bypassed (explicitly disable prefix/KV cache in runtime flags); 4) Compare outputs with token-diff, normalized edit distance, and embedding cosine similarity; 5) Repeat with a quantized kernel change or new compilation; 6) Observe and log cases where cache-hits cause non-trivial semantic or surface-form changes.
test_plan:
- Golden set: start with 1k anonymized prompts stratified by length and temperature; expand to domain-specific sets (emails, code, customer prompts) over time.
- Metrics: token_mismatch_rate, avg_embedding_distance (use base embedding model), pct_topk_logit_change_above_threshold.
- Thresholds: initial soft alert at embedding_dist>0.08 or token_mismatch_rate>2%, hard fail at embedding_dist>0.18 or token_mismatch_rate>5%.
- Automation: nightly job that runs across recent commits + each canary deploy run. PR check: sample 200 prompts, fail-safe if >1% exceed hard thresholds.
- Visualization: time-series on Console, and per-deploy histogram of delta scores.
- Regression lab: save offending examples with full trace and runtime flags to S3 for post-mortem.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1): prototype harness + local replay tooling, run against recent release candidates; Phase 2 (week 2-3): integrate as a job in CI and nightly runner, add Console panels; Phase 3 (week 4): wire alerts and canary gating so a canary deploy with cache changes is auto-aborted on hard failures; Phase 4: expand golden sets and per-customer gating for high-risk tenants.
mitigation:
- Quick toggle: runtime flag to forcibly bypass KV/prefix cache per route/tenant (already supported by runtime - ensure accessible to SRE).
- Cache versioning: tag cache artifacts so older safe cache behavior can be restored per-deploy.
- Canary policy: conservative rollout (10% traffic) with automatic rollback when harness triggers hard fail.
- Fallback model variant: route to dense (non-quantized) variant on failure to isolate quantization vs cache issues.
notes:
- Related design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/KV+Cache+Audit+Design (placeholder).
- Prototype scripts: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/kv-audit-proto (link in PRs).
- This ticket intentionally focuses on detection+operationalization; separate follow-ups will implement root-cause fixes in runtime kernels.
- Privacy: ensure trace anonymization pipeline runs before using production prompts.
